film

The Virgin Suicides

directed by Sofia Coppola, USA 1999, 96'
  • Sofia Coppola’s legendary directorial debut, which opened the door to the world of girlhood secrets, returns to Polish cinemas!
    • The Virgin Suicides is an adaptation of the cult novel by Jeffrey Eugenides, which has been published several times in Poland. The story of the five Lisbon sisters tells a tale of first times and entering adulthood—an adulthood that is impossible to escape (or is it?).
  • Phenomenally shot by Ed Lachman and featuring an ethereal soundtrack by the duo Air, The Virgin Suicides is a sensual coming-of-age story set in the 1970s. A quarter of a century later, this decade—bathed in saturated, sun-drenched colors—remains above all a memory and a fantasy, recorded in abandoned diaries, cut-down trees, and the sounds of vinyl records. The teenage Lisbon sisters are remembered by an unnamed narrator, who years ago fell in love not so much with one of the girls, but with the aura of mystery they projected around themselves.
    • The Virgin Suicides features a multi-generational cast of actors with a distinctive presence: James Woods (Videodrome), Kathleen Turner (Body Heat), and, above all, the very young Kirsten Dunst (Interview with the Vampire, Marie Antoinette) and Josh Hartnett (Pearl Harbor, Sin City). The film's airy, dreamy style was inspired by Picnic at Hanging Rock, making Coppola's debut look like Peter Weir's mysterious story transposed to the realities of American suburbs.
  • Generations of girls and women who share the sensibility captured in the film grew up on The Virgin Suicides. The production support of American Zoetrope—Francis Ford Coppola’s company—and the freedom of Sofia's imagination resulted in one of the breakthrough debuts of contemporary cinema: an intimate, yet unsettling story, scented with warm summer, in which one can fully immerse and lose oneself.
